title: Missing null check in formatValue can cause type coercion issues

evidence.quote:
if (value === undefined || value === null) return ''
  const u = unit || ''

reasoning: The function checks for undefined/null but then immediately uses 'value' without re-checking. If value is 0, the function works correctly, but the loose equality check pattern suggests the author may have intended to handle falsy values differently. More critically, the function accepts 'number | undefined' but the null check is redundant since TypeScript types don't include null.
recommendation: Remove the redundant null check and rely on TypeScript's type system: 'if (value === undefined) return '''. Alternatively, if null values are expected from runtime data, update the type signature to 'number | undefined | null'.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this feature. The type mismatch between runtime checks and TypeScript signature could cause confusion during maintenance.
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test formatValue with undefined, null, 0, negative numbers, and large numbers to verify consistent behavior.
